Let me analyze this certificate.

Certificate details:
- Number: R76/2006-DK3-17.22
- Member State: Denmark
- Issuing authority: DELTA, address Venlighedsvej 4, 2970 Hørsholm, Denmark
- Person responsible: J. Hovgård Jensen, Certification Manager
- Phone: +45 7219 4000
- Email: legal@delta.dk
- Website: www.madebydelta.com
- OIML issuer ID: DK3
- Date issued: 13 December 2017 → 2017-12-13
- Scheme: A (OIML-CS scheme A for certificates of conformity issued before... actually scheme A is the old one; certificates like this are Scheme A). The schema says scheme (A|B). This cert is from 2017, issued under the old OIML certificate system which is now Scheme A. I'll use "A".
- Project number: not explicitly present. Hmm, "project_number" — not present, omit.

Applicant: Tscale Electronics Mfg (Kunshan) Co., Ltd., address No.99 Shunchang Road, Zhoushi, Kunshan, Jiangsu, China

Manufacturer: same as applicant.

Certified type:
- Category: Non-automatic weighing instrument → per schema examples, categories like "Load cell", "Indicator"... For NA WIs, category would be "Non-automatic weighing instrument" — maybe "Weighing instrument". I'll use "Non-automatic weighing instrument".
- type_designations: ZTP, ZSP, ZHW-2, ZHW-7, ZHW-20, ZHC, WTP, WSP, USP, UTP, UHP, UHPS, UTW-2, UTW-7, UTW-20, UTC
- module_designation: Not applicable (whole instrument, not a module). Actually for R76 full instrument, "Not applicable" per schema.
- description: null (characteristics set out on page 2).

Recommendation: R76, edition 2006, scheme A, accuracy_classes ["III"].

Test reports: "tests described in the associated test reports from DELTA, DK, No. DANAK-1915746, dated 26-10-2015 that includes 71 pages" → id: "DANAK-1915746", date: 2015-10-26, pages: 71, role: test_report.

Characteristics table:
- Accuracy class: III → type_level: accuracy_class? Actually accuracy class is in recommendation. But could include in type_level as accuracy_class: "III".
- Weighing range: Single-interval or multi-interval → this varies... "weighing_range_configurations" — could be a string "Single-interval or multi-interval". This is a config axis but only one attribute; keep as type_level string.
- Maximum capacity Max_i: 3 kg to 30 kg → {min: 3, max: 30}, unit kg
- Minimum capacity Min_i: 20 e_i → value "20 e" — formula/symbol → value: 20, unit? "20 e_i" is 20 × e. Keep as string "20 e" with footnote... Better: value: "20 e", unit_symbol null. Rule says formulas/symbols keep as string. I'll do value: "20 e" — hmm, "20 e_i". Let me write value: "20e" — no, keep "20 e". Actually canonical: minimum_capacity: {value: "20e", ...}. I'll use "20 e".
- Verification scale interval e_i: ≥ 0.5 g → {min: 0.5, max: null}, unit g
- Number of intervals Max/e: 3000 (single-interval), 2×3000 (multi-interval) → config_level with axis "interval_type": conditions "single-interval" → 3000, "multi-interval" → "2×3000" (6000). Value could be 6000. Keep "2×3000" as string? The value is 2×3000 = 6000 intervals across two partial ranges. I'd record value 3000 for single, 6000 for multi with note, or string. I'll use config_level:
  - attribute: number_of_intervals, axis: weighing_range_type, values: [{condition: "single-interval", value: 3000}, {condition: "multi-interval", value: "2×3000"}]
- Subtractive tare T: ≤ -Max → hmm, subtractive tare typically "=-Max" ... The cell says "≤ -Max"? Actually likely "=- Max". Keep as string "-Max" → value: "-Max"? The marker is ≤? For subtractive tare, capacity of tare = Max. I'll record value string "=-Max"... I'll do value: "-Max" — hmm, safer: value: "≤ -Max" as string? Per rule 2, formulas kept as strings. I'll use value: "Max" with... no. Let me just record subtractive_tare_limit: {value: "-Max"}. Hmm. I think value: "=-Max"? The markdown says "≤ -Max". I'll use value: "-Max", unit null. Actually to not fabricate, keep "≤ -Max"? The ≤ here likely means the tare range extends up to -Max. I'll record value as string "-Max". Hmm, I'll keep it as "=-Max"? No — don't alter. Value: "≤ -Max"... That includes symbol ≤. I think "−Max" string is fine: "value": "-Max".

Let me just use "value": "-Max" with unit null.

- Interface: Protective, according to paragraph 5.3.6 → interface: {value: "Protective", ...} maybe a separate note. Record interface_type: {value: "Protective"} and interface_reference: "paragraph 5.3.6"? Simpler: interface: {value: "Protective, according to paragraph 5.3.6"}. I'll do that as string.
- Supply voltage: 12 VDC / 100-240 VAC, 50/60 Hz using external AC/DC; 6V rechargeable battery (optional)
  Split:
  - dc_supply_voltage: 12 V
  - ac_supply_voltage: {min:100, max:240} V
  - power_supply_frequency: {min:50, max:60} Hz
  - battery_voltage: 6 V, optional battery — condition. Record battery_supply_voltage: 6 V with note? There's no footnote system for this; keep simple: battery_voltage: {value: 6, unit_symbol: "V"}.
- Temperature range: -10 °C / +40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit °C
- Software identification: legal relevant software 1.11; application software 01.xx(y)
  - legal_relevant_software_identification: "1.11"
  - application_software_identification: "01.xx(y)"

Model family: multiple type designations — 16 types. Do they have varying characteristics? Not specified; Max range 3–30 kg applies to family. The schema says model_family include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. There are 16 type designations. We could create models entries per type designation. That's reasonable: model_family.models with model_id each type. But no per-model attributes given. I'll include model_family with family_name null and models list of the 16 types. Hmm — the ranges like Max 3–30 kg likely vary by model but not stated. Including models list seems right since cert covers >1 model.

Type designations: ZTP, ZSP, ZHW-2, ZHW-7, ZHW-20, ZHC, WTP, WSP, USP, UTP, UHP, UHPS, UTW-2, UTW-7, UTW-20, UTC.

Count: ZTP, ZSP, ZHW-2, ZHW-7, ZHW-20, ZHC (6), WTP, WSP (8), USP, UTP, UHP, UHPS, UTW-2, UTW-7, UTW-20, UTC (16).

Model ids: use those strings.

Revision history: not present, omit.

Footnotes: none.
